_doc: The LLM Adapter contract (B2). What the APEX runtime REQUIRES from whatever model runs underneath, a per-provider capability matrix, and the graceful-degradation rules. This is the hardware-abstraction layer: the kernel (SKILL.md + scripts) stays stable while the model under it changes. Read/edited by humans; loaded by scripts/llm_adapter.py (stdlib json, no PyYAML).

tool_calling.why: the runtime invokes scripts/*.py as tools; without it, scripts are run manually and results pasted back

subprocess_exec.why: PoT / RK4 / stances run in isolated subprocesses (harness-provided, not the model itself)

structured_json_output.why: stances emit {answer,confidence}; directors emit SHA-256 laudos as JSON

multi_turn.why: snapshot + memory recall let a session resume across turns/interruptions

subagents.why: Level-B parallel cognition (real concurrent instances); absence degrades to Level-A subprocess PoT

long_context.why: the heavy modes want more window; a small window caps the mode, it does not break the runtime

claude.notes: reference runtime; native Agent subagents give real Level-B parallelism

gpt.notes: function calling present; no native subagent fan-out -> Level-A parallelism

local.notes: small OSS model; sequential PoT, best-effort JSON, mode is capped

degradation_rules.action: force parallelism Level A (concurrent_executor subprocess PoT); ignore spawn_subagents manifests
run scripts manually and paste their output back; PoT becomes copy-run-paste; no automatic tool loop
parse the LAST JSON-looking line of the output; wrap stance/laudo prompts with an explicit 'print exactly one JSON object' and validate before merging
cap the mode to the largest one whose window fits; announce the downgrade instead of silently truncating
